title: False Assurance: How AI Readers Use Source-Check Verdicts on Community Notes
description:
Community Notes checks whether a note looks sourced, not whether the cited page supports the claim. We test how three chat LLMs (Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Haiku 5.5, Gemini 3.8 Flash) use a source-check verdict that can be wrong, with and without the passage the checker read, on 80 real Helpful notes (1,920 answers). With a verdict only, the readers inherited the checker's errors; the checked passage protected against false alarms but rarely against false assurances. A page-level check of 200 paired AI-written and human-written Helpful notes found that 52 to 68% of readable cited pages do not fully support the claim.

This release contains the report (paper/report.pdf), code, prompts, tests, preregistration with dated amendments, result files and public data. Apart Research AI x Epistemics Research Sprint, November 2026.
